reasoning: In the last 45 days I could not find any reputable, state-specific general-election polling for a 2026 New York Senate race or for a 2026 presidential contest in New York; available recent polls and coverage focus instead on the 2026 governor’s race, plus some national presidential primary polling that is not state-specific.[2][8][12][15] Because none of these sources directly measure New York’s current 2026 Senate or presidential margins, they must be treated as contextual only and cannot support a quantified D+ or R+ margin for those races under your rules. Structurally, Cook’s updated PVI indicates New York is a strongly Democratic-leaning state (approximately D+12 statewide), but that is a long-term index rather than a current-race polling margin.[1][3][5][6]

sources.name: New York Post / Red Oak Strategic
sources.details: Red Oak Strategic poll (reported by New York Post) found Gov. Kathy Hochul leading Republican Bruce Blakeman 47%-43% among registered New York voters, a Hochul +4 governor margin.

sources.name: Siena College (via WLT Report summary)
sources.details: Siena College poll cited in coverage showed Hochul leading Blakeman 52%-32% among New York registered voters, a Hochul +20 governor margin earlier in the cycle.

sources.name: Siena Research Institute (reported by La Nación)
sources.details: Siena Research Institute survey of 811 likely New York voters found Hochul at 49% and Blakeman at 39% in the governor’s race, a Hochul +10 margin, with independents narrowly favoring Blakeman.

sources.name: Politico / Siena University
sources.details: Politico report on Siena University poll notes Hochul leads Blakeman by 10 points in the first major likely-voter poll of the New York governor’s race this cycle.

sources.name: Emerson College (via Washington Times)
sources.details: Emerson College July 2026 national poll reported Democratic figures including New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in a national presidential field, but did not provide New York state-specific 2026 presidential general-election margins.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – 2026 PVI (via summary)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s updated Partisan Voting Index for 2026 classifies New York as a strongly Democratic-leaning state, approximately D+12 statewide, reflecting its average presidential performance vs. the national vote.
